MindScape3D Fix List

MindScape3D fix list

Everything asked for in the capstone list, grouped by area, with the screenshot each note points at and a plan for each one. 38 items: 3 bugs, 25 changes, 8 new features, 2 questions. Plans are sized small (6), medium (16), large (14) and extra large (2). Tick items off as you go; your ticks stay in this browser only.

0 of 38 checked

Filters

Things in the list that clash with the game as it is now

  • Breathing exercise. The objectives describe a four-count inhale and six-count exhale. The exercise was changed to 15 seconds with a 5 / 3 / 7 pattern on request, so one of the two needs updating.
  • Third person. The objectives call the game third-person. Scrolling to first person (F03) would be an extra view, not a replacement.
  • Thought Courtroom. The objectives name it, and the game ships it as the Worry Courtroom.
  • Undertale music. The tracks are copyrighted, so a public release needs permission or a royalty-free substitute.

Suggested build order

Phases run roughly in this order. Sizes are rough: small is under half a day, medium about a day, large two to four days, extra large a week or more, for one developer and not counting art made outside Unity.

  1. Phase 0Decide first4 items

    Questions and choices that block other work: the reset method, the meaning of “animated”, the music plan, and the remaining Chapter 1 notes.

    F01F02F04F10
  2. Phase 1Foundations6 items

    Movement, camera and interaction fixes that everything else rests on.

    F03F05F06F07F08F09
  3. Phase 2Quick content wins6 items

    Small, self-contained changes that are visible right away.

    F11F12F14F16F23F28
  4. Phase 3Story build15 items

    The larger Chapter 1 to 3 scenes that need animation, travel and new rooms.

    F13F15F17F18F19F20F21F22F24F25F26F27F29F30F31
  5. Phase 4Ending7 items

    Chapter 3 Episode 8 and the final scenes, which need music, sketch art and the younger self.

    F32F33F34F35F36F37F38

Shared building blocks

Several items need the same tool. Build each once and the items it unlocks get smaller.

B1Collision and camera fixes

Fix movement snags and the camera inside the body first. Every later camera or room change depends on a player who can move and a camera that behaves.

Unlocks: F06, F07, F08, F09

B2Player animation set

The player only has idle, walk and run. Add lying down, sleeping, sitting up, taking out a photo and talking gestures once, then reuse them. First check whether the rig can use retargeted clips or the clips need to be made in Blender.

Unlocks: F19, F20, F26, F29, F31

B3Cinematic helper

AcademicEpisode already has Shot, Glide, Fade and the flashback frame. Wrap them into one helper (glide, fade, flashback, line) so every animated moment uses the same tool.

Unlocks: F05, F16, F18, F25, F34, F38

B4Travel sequence

Turn the house-to-bus-stop-to-bus code in HouseEpisode into a reusable journey (marker route, bus, arrival), so trips between home, school and the venue are built once.

Unlocks: F13, F15, F17, F21

B5Scene music director

One change in MusicManager: a scene-to-track map, crossfades and fade-outs.

Unlocks: F10, F11, F33, F38

B6Outfit system

A small system that swaps the player's clothes by id and remembers it across scenes.

Unlocks: F22, F21

Account and project questions

F01 Question PDF p.1

Login without verification: where does a password reset go?

Is it OK that creating an account needs no email, Gmail, Facebook or similar verification? Once deployed, if a player forgets their password, where would the reset button lead? The list asks how other login systems handle this.

NoteAs built, accounts are username + password only and no email is stored, so a reset has nowhere to send a link. This needs a decision: a recovery code shown at sign-up, a security question, or a manual reset.

Plan

MPhase 0
  1. Decide the reset method first. Recommended: a recovery code shown once at sign-up. Other options: a security question, or no reset (the player makes a new account). Email is not needed for any of these.
  2. Add a recovery code to the account (Supabase migration; only a hash is stored). register_player returns the code once.
  3. Show a “Save your recovery code” panel after Create account on the Welcome page, with a copy button.
  4. Add a reset_password RPC (username + code + new password) with a limit on wrong tries, and a “Forgot password?” link on the Welcome panel that opens a small reset form.
  5. Say clearly on the sign-up text that there is no email, so a lost code cannot be recovered.
Where
Assets/Database/MindscapeCloud.csMainMenuNew.uxmlMainMenuNewController.csSupabase migration
Needs from you
  • Adviser's answer on the reset method
Check
Register, reset with the code, log in with the new password; five wrong codes lock the reset for a while; offline play unchanged.

Camera, controls and interaction

F03 NewPartly done PDF p.2

Scroll to switch from third person to first person

Let the player scroll to move the camera between third-person and first-person.

NoteThe project objectives describe a third-person game, so first person is an optional extra view. Done: scrolling in past the closest distance blends to first person (eye height, body hidden through ShotFocus) and scrolling out returns. Added 2026-10-21 for mobile: a VIEW button above the look stick in the touch overlay, and a First-person view toggle under Options > General next to Mobile controls. Every way of switching saves the choice (PlayerPrefs), so the next scene starts in the same view. Still open: pinch to zoom on phones, and a walk-through in each scene (compiled, not yet played in the editor).

Plan

MPhase 1Needs first: F06, F07
  1. Scrolling already zooms the third-person camera (minDistance 2.5). Let it continue in to about 0.
  2. Below roughly 0.8 the camera becomes first person: it sits at eye height, looks along yaw and pitch, and drops the shoulder offset.
  3. Hide the player's body in first person (shadow stays), reusing the hide logic in ShotFocus. Use a small near-clip plane while in this mode.
  4. Scroll back out to return to third person, with a short blend. Remember the last mode in PlayerPrefs. Add pinch on mobile.
  5. Interaction works by distance (E and F prompts), so it should carry over; check that the prompts and the crosshair still read well in first person.

Movement and collision bugs

F06 Bug PDF p.4

Player gets stuck when pressing against objects or the house

When the character moves right up against objects or the house, it cannot move any more.

Plan

MPhase 1
  1. Reproduce it: log OnControllerColliderHit while pressing into walls, kerbs and corners in the house and street, to find which colliders trap the player.
  2. Tune the CharacterController: skin width up to about 0.08 (it is 0.02), step offset up to about 0.5 (it is 0.3).
  3. Move horizontally and vertically in one Move call so the controller slides along surfaces instead of stopping.
  4. Replace trapping mesh colliders (kerbs, wall edges) with simple box colliders in the builders (HouseModelSync, WorldModelSync).
  5. Add an unstick fallback: if input is held and the player has not moved for about a second, push out along the contact normal. A last-safe position already exists.
Where
Assets/PlayerMovement.csAssets/Editor/HouseModelSync.csworld model sync
Needs from you
  • Nothing
Check
Hold a direction against every wall, corner and kerb in the house and street for 10 s each and still be able to walk away.

F07 Bug PDF p.4

Camera ends up inside the character

While examining the books (“My reference books and research notes”) the camera sits inside the character's head and the view is blocked.

Plan

SPhase 1
  1. Cause: ShotOver puts the camera “back” units from the target toward the player. When the player stands next to the target, the camera ends up inside the body, and ShotFocus only hides the body when it blocks the line.
  2. In Shot(), if the camera is inside or within about 0.9 m of the player's capsule, either push it out along the away-from-player direction or hide the body at once.
  3. Use a small near-clip plane for story shots.
  4. Add an editor check that walks every Spot in every episode and fails if its shot starts inside the player.
Where
Assets/AcademicPressure/AcademicEpisode.csAssets/ShotFocus.cs
Needs from you
  • Nothing
Check
Examine the books, bag, plate and bed from several standing positions; the view is never inside the character.
